next.review: Counts only until the FIRST LOOK at 60 complete forward days (240 rows), the SECOND at 120, then one non-overlapping look per 60: improvement over the HARD baseline (HAR-X + clock + the last-30-minute range + the range so far: two plain persistence terms that already capture 79 percent of the gain over HAR-X + clock) with a week-block 95 percent CI, both halves and a circular-shift placebo (docs/STRUCTURE_SHADOW_MODEL_DESIGN_20261105.md).
next.ifConfirmed: CI lower bound above 0 and both halves positive: keep it as the next-hour range display; no consumer is wired without the user's word.
next.ifFailed: At the SECOND look the CI includes 0 or the estimate is negative: retire to the HAR-X + clock baseline and write the autopsy (which decision time and which group lost skill).

notes: HONESTY CHECK (2026-11-05): two plain persistence terms (the last-30-minute range and the range so far) added to HAR-X + clock already capture 79 percent of the model's gain over HAR-X + clock; the replay edge over that HARD baseline is about +6.5 percent, not tested with an interval. The forward looks are judged against the hard baseline.

The explore-era series is a WALK-FORWARD replay: every row was predicted by a model fitted only on earlier days (out-of-sample by construction), but the features were chosen on this same era, so it is a lead (pre-registered test: claim structure_model_stepA_20261104), not forward evidence.
It forecasts a RANGE (volatility), not a direction, and nothing trades or gates on it.
Forward rows start with the first nightly run after the build; until then the card shows the explore replay only.
